paper_sections.title: Structure of orbitofrontal cortex and its longitudinal course in cancer-related post-traumatic stress disorder
Assessment of PTSD symptomatic responses to the cancer experience
Comparison of gray matter volume between breast cancer survivors with PTSD and those without PTSD or healthy subjects at the baseline investigation
Correlation of right BA11 gray matter volume with PTSD symptomatic responses
Longitudinal course of right BA11 gray matter volume in breast cancer survivors with PTSD compared to the course in survivors without PTSD

description.value: The study investigated structural brain alterations associated with cancer-related PTSD in breast cancer survivors and examined the longitudinal course of gray matter volume over two years.

design.value: Baseline and two-year follow-up structural MRI study of breast cancer survivors with PTSD, breast cancer survivors without PTSD, and healthy subjects, using voxel-based morphometry for cross-sectional comparisons and repeated-measures mixed-model analyses for longitudinal effects.

description.value: A self-reported questionnaire consisting of 15 items: 7 items assessing intrusion symptoms and 8 items assessing avoidance symptoms. Each item is rated using a 4-point scale (“not at all” = 0, “rarely” = 1, “sometimes” = 3, “often” = 5).

name.value: Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV Axis I Disorders (SCID), Clinician Version

description.value: A semi-structured interview used by a trained psychiatrist to assess psychiatric diagnoses, including current PTSD.
Cognitive impairment was defined as a score of less than 24.

name.value: performance status defined by the Eastern Cooperative Groups

description.value: Used to assess moderate physical symptoms that interfered with daily life.
Female breast cancer survivors aged 18 to 55 years who met criteria for cancer-related PTSD; 14 participated at baseline and 9 were available at follow-up.

medical_condition.value: breast cancer survivors with cancer-related post-traumatic stress disorder

diagnostic_instrument.value: Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV Axis I Disorders (SCID)

clinical_characteristics.value: 14 (12%) met the criteria for PTSD (current: 4 and past: 10).

medication_status.value: All were antidepressant-naive; at follow-up all the patients with PTSD had recovered naturally without any pharmacological or psychological intervention.

inclusion_criteria.value: an age between 18 and 55 years during the recruitment periods
breast cancer surgery and survival for 3-15 months

exclusion_criteria.value: a history of treatment for cancer other than breast cancer or double cancer
clear evidence of residual or recurrent cancer
chemotherapy or radiation therapy within the previous month
psychotropic medication within the previous month
a history of any neurological disorder or traumatic brain injury accompanied by periods of unconsciousness
a history of substance abuse or dependence
cognitive impairment defined as a score of less than 24 on the Mini-Mental State Examination

description.value: Breast cancer survivors who did not meet criteria for PTSD; 100 participated at baseline and 67 were available at follow-up.

clinical_characteristics.value: Of the other 100 patients, 12 (12%) have met 1 or 2 PTSD criteria of reexperience, avoidance, and hyperarousal symptoms in the past.

description.value: Healthy subjects who lived in the geographic area of the National Cancer Center and met the eligibility criteria used for cancer patients except for the requirement of a history of breast cancer surgery.

recruitment_method.value: advertisements or flyers in the local newspaper

task_description.value: Structural MRI scans were obtained at baseline and two years later in a longitudinal investigation of gray matter volume.

instrument.value: Signa Scanner; GE Medical Systems, Milwaukee, Wisconsin

description.value: Three-dimensional spoiled gradient-recalled acquisition of 1.5-mm contiguous sections.

An optimized voxel-based morphometry method was used. A customized template set was created, scans were spatially normalized, smoothed, averaged to create a customized template, segmented into gray and white matter, modulated to correct for volume changes during normalization, and smoothed again.

steps.value: created an optimized study-specific template set consisting of a T1 image and a priori gray, white, and cerebrospinal fluid images
spatially normalized all scans to the customized template
smoothed with an 8-mm, full-width maximum (FWHM) smoothing kernel
segmented into gray matter and white matter, using customized prior probability maps
modulated to correct for volume changes occurring during spatial normalization
smoothed using a 12-mm FWHM Gaussian kernel

description.value: As to the amygdala and hippocampus, 4-mm FWHM smoothing was performed and then the same procedure as above was followed.

model_type.value: analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) with a basic SPM2 model

model_settings.value: Age, accumulated alcohol consumption, and total gray matter volume were entered as nuisance variables. Significance levels were set at a p-value of 0.05 and corrected for multiple comparisons using the false discovery rate approach in regions without a hypothesis. For hypothesized regions, significance was assumed at an uncorrected p-value of 0.001 and a k-value of 100. A small volume correction was applied to the bilateral ACC and OFC.

Correlation analysis between regional brain volume and the IES score controlling for age, accumulated alcohol consumption, and total gray matter volume. Significance levels were set at p < 0.05 (two-tailed).

software.value: SPSS software 14.0J; MarsBaR ROI analysis toolbox

model_type.value: repeated measures mixed model analysis of covariance

model_settings.value: TIME (baseline vs. follow-up), DIAGNOSIS (PTSD vs. non-PTSD), and TIME × DIAGNOSIS were used as effects on brain volume within the ROI. Covariates were age, accumulated alcohol consumption, total gray matter volume at baseline, and days from baseline to follow-up. Significance levels were set at p < 0.05 (two-tailed).

description.value: Scans taken 3-15 months after breast cancer surgery.
Scans performed 2 years after the first scan.

name.value: Comparison of gray matter volume between breast cancer survivors with PTSD and those without PTSD at the baseline investigation

roi_definition.value: regions with a hypothesis (amygdala, hippocampus, ACC, and OFC)

definition.value: smaller gray matter volume in breast cancer survivors with PTSD than in those without PTSD

correction_scope.value: regions with a hypothesis; bilateral ACC and OFC for SVC

model_representation_notes.value: Age, accumulated alcohol consumption, and total gray matter volume were included as nuisance variables.

interpretations.value: The right OFC gray matter volume might play an important role in the pathophysiology of PTSD.

definition.value: smaller gray matter volume in breast cancer survivors with PTSD than in healthy subjects

correction_scope.value: regions with a hypothesis; bilateral ACC and OFC for SVC

name.value: Correlation of right BA11 gray matter volume with total IES score

roi_definition.value: areas detected to be significantly smaller in cancer survivors with PTSD than in those without PTSD at baseline

definition.value: negative correlation between right BA11 gray matter volume and the total IES score

interpretations.value: A smaller OFC gray matter volume might reflect the difficulty of cancer survivors with PTSD in extricating fear-conditioned emotional memories of their cancer experience.

name.value: Correlation of right BA11 gray matter volume with Intrusion subscale score

roi_definition.value: areas detected to be significantly smaller in cancer survivors with PTSD than in those without PTSD at baseline

definition.value: negative correlation between right BA11 gray matter volume and the Intrusion subscale score

interpretations.value: The OFC might play an important role in the pathophysiology of PTSD, particularly its intrusive symptoms.

name.value: Interaction of TIME and GROUP on right BA11 gray matter volume in breast cancer survivors

roi_definition.value: ROI detected in the baseline voxel-based morphometry analysis

definition.value: the interaction between TIME (baseline vs. follow-up) and DIAGNOSIS (PTSD vs. non-PTSD) on right BA11 gray matter volume

model_representation_notes.value: TIME, DIAGNOSIS, and TIME × DIAGNOSIS were modeled, with age, accumulated alcohol consumption, total gray matter volume at baseline, and days from baseline to follow-up as covariates.

interpretations.value: The OFC gray matter volume may remain constant after the development of cancer-related PTSD.

name.value: Right BA11 gray matter volume of cancer survivors with PTSD compared with cancer survivors without PTSD at follow-up

roi_definition.value: ROI detected in the baseline voxel-based morphometry analysis

definition.value: the right BA11 gray matter volume of the cancer survivors with PTSD was significantly smaller than that of cancer survivors without PTSD at the follow-up investigation

interpretations.value: The smaller right BA11 size might have existed before the development of cancer-related PTSD or might have occurred as a result of scarring from the cancer-related PTSD.
